title: Best Product Designers (2026): How to Hire an Industrial Designer
description: How to hire an industrial or product designer for a physical product: what to include, prototypes, manufacturing, rights, price factors and red flags.
intro: Industrial designers shape physical products: how they look, feel and work, and how they can be manufactured. They create sketches, 3D models and technical files for prototypes and factories. Product design projects go wrong when the design cannot be made at a reasonable cost, the files are not ready for manufacturers, or ownership of the design is unclear. This guide helps you move from idea to a design you can actually produce.

faq.q: What does an industrial designer deliver?
faq.a: Typically sketches, 3D CAD models, renders and files for prototyping, such as 3D printing, and sometimes manufacturing drawings.
Almost always. A prototype shows how the product feels and works, and reveals problems that drawings cannot.

faq.q: Will the design be ready for manufacturing?
faq.a: Ask specifically. Designing for manufacturing involves materials, tolerances and production methods. Many projects need a manufacturer's input before final files.

faq.q: How do I protect my idea?
faq.a: Use a confidentiality agreement and confirm you own the design. For patents or design registration, consult a qualified professional.
Many products must meet safety rules, such as for electrical items or children's products. Check the requirements for your product and market.
